content:
alice: onboarding hit: `pip install redwood-inference-sdk` fails on M1 laptops, pip tries to build from sdist and then errors out on a rust compile step. any quick fixes?

- dmitri: yeah this is the wheel gap. We only publish manylinux x86_64. macos arm64 users get sdist -> rust compile.

- anya: reproducible with poetry 1.4 too: `poetry add redwood-inference-sdk` makes a lock that pulls a newer `typing-extensions` incompatible with our pinned range.

- alice: new hire can't proceed with the quickstart sample app :(

- dmitri: short term: tell them to `pip install --prefer-binary redwood-inference-sdk` or install rust toolchain. Long term: publish macos wheels (universal2 or arm64).

- packaging-bot: created PKG-230: add macos arm64 wheel builds using cibuildwheel.

- anya: also propose we add `[project.optional-dependencies]
async = ["aiohttp>=3.8"]` so async users opt in. stops unnecessary heavy deps on install.

- dmitri: +1. And add `typing-extensions` with a compatible range in pyproject to avoid poetry lock conflicts.

- ci-bot: suggestion: add sample-app smoke job that runs `pip install --no-cache-dir redwood-inference-sdk` on macos-latest to catch regressions.

- alice: i'll update onboarding docs with `--prefer-binary` note and open a ticket linking PKG-230. assigning: dmitri -> CI & wheels, anya -> pyproject change.

- dmitri: i'll add GH action matrix for macos and run `cibuildwheel --platform macos` to produce universal2 and arm64 wheels, then test installing the produced wheel on a mac runner.

- anya: will prepare a tiny patch relaxing typing-extensions and adding extras. will also add a README note about `poetry add "redwood-inference-sdk[async]"`.

- alice: thanks team. once wheels publish i'll verify by spinning a fresh venv on an M1 runner and close the onboarding blocker. :raised_hands:
